subject: CareWise: plan chooser impact matrix and bundle mapping
messages:
From: Aisha Bryant <aisha.bryant@carewise.io>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@carewise.io
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify upgrade window + bundle mapping for pilot -> production

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at CareWise is excited about Redwood's latency profile and the embedding reranking features. Before we lock internal approvals, procurement has asked for a clear mapping of: (1) what changes if we move from the pilot compact plan to a production throughput tier, (2) which features are bundled vs add-ons, and (3) what the upgrade/proration window looks like (pricing and credits).

Specifically: can you show an example scenario where we run the pilot (60k monthly tokens + embeddings) then scale to a 3x throughput reserved capacity with burst and prefix-caching? We need a short matrix we can include in the internal procurement memo.

We'd also like to see any discounts tied to a 12-month committed purchase and whether the quantization option is included or billed separately.

Can you put something together by Friday so I can route it to finance?

Best,
Aisha Bryant
Head of Integrations, CareWise
Aisha.Bryant@carewise.io

--
Attachment: current-pilot-stats.csv (attachment stub)

From: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Bryant <aisha.bryant@carewise.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify upgrade window + bundle mapping for pilot -> production

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Ben (pricing) and Evelyn (customer success) to build a concise matrix.

High-level plan:
- We will produce a two-page matrix: pilot baseline, three scale scenarios (1.5x, 3x reserved, 3x reserved + burst).
- For each scenario we show: seat/throughput equivalence, expected per-token unit cost, embedding batch pricing, and which features remain included (KV/prefix cache, model quantization options, monitoring retention).
- Upgrade mechanics: prorated billing for reserved capacity purchases; credits applied for unused pilot committed tokens (if pilot was billed as prepay credits).
- Discounts: standard 12-month commit tiered discount (5% at 50k/mo commit, 10% at 250k/mo commit) plus case-by-case multi-year concessions.

Ben — can you draft the pricing column and a short paragraph on quantization (is it a free config on dedicated vs a paid conversion service)?
Evelyn — can you add the operational steps (what we need from CareWise to schedule cutover and cache warming)?

We will send the matrix + annotated SOW by Friday EOD. If carewise wants faster turnaround we can prioritize the 3x scenario only.

Naomi Feldman
Director, Mid-Market Sales
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

Attachment: request-pilot-stats.csv (from Aisha)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: Aisha Bryant <aisha.bryant@carewise.io>, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify upgrade window + bundle mapping for pilot -> production

Thanks Naomi — drafting numbers below. Quick notes in-line.

--- Pricing snapshot (example scenarios) ---
Scenario A — Pilot (current): 60k tokens/month generation + embeddings (light). Billed as usage credits.
Scenario B — Production 1.5x reserved: 90k tokens/mo reserved + on-demand burst.
Scenario C — Production 3x reserved: 180k tokens/mo reserved, prioritized capacity (SLA).
Scenario D — 3x reserved + burst: 180k reserved + defined burst pool (ads-hoc).

Assumptions: average generation token cost baseline $0.0007/token (hosted), embedding unit $0.0025/embedding. Reserved pricing reduces per-token by ~18% for 1.5x, 28% for 3x (after commit discount).

Discounts: 12-month commit = base tier discount (see table):
- 50k/mo: 5%
- 150k/mo: 8%
- 250k+ /yr: 10% + negotiation margin (possible 12% with multi-year).

Quantization: on Dedicated/Private, customers can apply our standard 8-bit quantization profile (no extra monthly fee) but if Redwood performs an engineering conversion to a custom quantized model we charge a one-time conversion fee (typical range $5k–$15k depending on model and validation).

Upgrade / proration flow:
- If customer upgrades mid-billing-cycle to reserved capacity, we prorate remaining days and apply a credit for consumed usage vs reserved commitment.
- If pilot was pre-paid credits, we apply a top-up invoice and credit any remaining pilot credits to the first reserved invoice.

Attachments I'm preparing: pack-impact-matrix.xlsx (matrix with numbers) and a short SOW draft that outlines cutover timeline and roles.

Question for CareWise: do you expect the quantization conversion to be included in the procurement approval, or should we treat it as an optional line item? That changes the SOW wording.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

--
Attachment: pack-impact-matrix.xlsx (draft)

From: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Bryant <aisha.bryant@carewise.io>, procurement@carewise.io
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify upgrade window + bundle mapping for pilot -> production

Aisha — attached is the package-impact matrix and an annotated SOW (CareWise_Renewal_SOW_v2.pdf). Highlights and ask for procurement:

- Recommendation: move to Scenario C (3x reserved) for predictable latency and priority capacity during business hours. Estimated blended per-token cost after 10% commit discount: $0.00050/token; embedding cost $0.0019/embedding.
- Bundling: KV/prefix caching, model monitoring (7d retention), and console routing tools included in the reserved package. Quantization remains an optional one-time conversion service (we've priced at $8k for the model family you use).
- Upgrade mechanics: we will prorate reserved commitment from purchase date; any pre-paid pilot credits will be automatically applied to the first invoice.
- Action items for CareWise to approve: accept SOW v2; confirm whether quantization conversion should be included as a line item; confirm target cutover week (we've penciled 2026-09-13).

Next steps: if procurement approves the SOW and quantization line item, legal will issue an amendment and finance will prepare the invoice. Evelyn, can you schedule a 30-minute cutover planning call with CareWise next Tuesday?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk through the matrix.

Naomi Feldman
Director, Mid-Market Sales
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
